title: Sprint 2 - Table Creation & Schema
description: Complete all MongoDB queries in this sprint.

tickets.title: Create the Users Collection
tickets.description:
We need a place to store our users. Create a collection named `users`.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    username TEXT NOT NULL,
    email TEXT NOT NULL
);
```
tasks: We need a place to store our users. Create a collection named `users`.
learning_objectives: Learn how to explicitly create a collection using `createCollection`.
common_mistakes: Using SQL CREATE TABLE syntax or using wrong casing for the collection name.

tickets.title: Create the Todos Collection
tickets.description:
Create the `todos` collection that will link to the `users` collection.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
CREATE TABLE todos (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    priority INTEGER DEFAULT 3,
    due_date DATE,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
);
```
tasks: Create the `todos` collection that will link to the `users` collection.
learning_objectives: Learn how to explicitly create a collection named `todos`.
common_mistakes: Using SQL CREATE TABLE syntax or wrong collection name.

tickets.title: UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT NULL Constraints
tickets.description:
Create a `categories` collection. (In MongoDB, validations are dynamic or defined as jsonSchema. For this task, explicitly create the collection).

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    color_code TEXT CHECK(color_code LIKE '#%')
);
```
tasks: Create a `categories` collection. (In MongoDB, validations are dynamic or defined as jsonSchema. For this task, explicitly create the collection).
learning_objectives: Understand explicit collection creation for categories.
